items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER: But like I tell you, man, Buster Bailey, Bushell -- you remember Garvin Bushell? ... MR. GREER: He played all the lead instruments.

ctx.x: And we had to be -- you know, it was necessary. We had to be twice as good as them guys, you know. Now you do--- for recognition. You had to be twice as good. Had to be twice as good singing, twice as good dancing, playing the music. It goes to show you. They say no greater compliment in the world than to be imitated, you know. They're all imitating. All of them want to be soul, soul brothers. That's a big joke. If you ain't got no soul you sure ain't going to be down here with your soul gone, you ain't going to…
But like I tell you, man, Buster Bailey, Bushell -- you remember Garvin Bushell?

items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: Sonny conspired to get everybody to quit the band, quit Snowden and brought them back the next night as Duke Ellington's band.

ctx.x: Well, how did that come out --

All right. Now, they had a job at the Kentucky Club and Sonny -- to this day, you know, Sonny Greer -- well, Duke took care of Sonny, (41) [Duke] the day he died. He paid him $100.00 a week. He fired him out of the band because Sonny was (unintelligible) liquor head he fired him out of the band, but he paid him $100.00 a week for the rest of his life. Sonny conspired to get everybody to quit the band, quit Snowden and brought them back the next night as Duke Ellington's band. You see, Snowden quit -- they all…
Sonny Greer planned it that way.
